newsitem.title: USA: Metallica calls feasibility study positive.
newsitem.headline: Metallica calls feasibility study positive.

text.p: Metallica Resources Inc said the final feasibility study for its 100 percent-owned Cerro San Pedro gold-silver project in central Mexico was positive.

"With this positive study, management is committed to moving quickly through permitting and financing to construction in order to commence commercial production within the next 18 months," chief executive Craig J. Nelsen said.
The company said the project's main parameters, as determined by the study, show:

-- Proven/Probable Reserves: 77.3 million metric tonnes of oxide ore grading 0.60 grams/tonne (g/t) gold and 24.8 g/t silver for a total of 1.5 million ounces gold and 62 million ounces silver, respectively
-- Global Resource: 250 million tonnes grading 0.49 g/t gold and 15.5 g/t silver for a total of 3.9 million ounces gold and 125 million ounces silver
-- Mining: open-pit at 30,000 tonnes/day ore, 1.51:1 average strip ratio over an eight year mine life
-- Processing: Heap leach/Merrill Crowe Plant, 74% gold recovery and 48 percent silver recovery
-- Average Production Cost: US$169/oz gold (treating silver revenue as a credit)
-- Average Annual Production Rates: 143,000 ounces gold and 3.8 million ounces silver
-- Projected Internal Rate of Return: 19.8 percent at $360/oz gold and $5.25 silver prices; and
-- Anticipated completion of mine permits and project financing is year-end 1997 with commercial production targeted for 1998's fourth quarter.
